newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar powers above 124 yen, four-year high in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Dollar powers above 124 yen, four-year high in Tokyo.

text.p: The dollar powered its way above the key 124 yen level, rising to 124.10 yen, a fresh four-year high, in Tokyo on Friday.
An increasing sense that this weekend's Group of Seven (G7) meeting will throw no obstacles in the way of even further dollar gains also kept buying interest strong.
In addition traders said there was heavy buying by foreign commercial banks, although the reasons were not immediately clear.
Fresh comments on Thursday from an array of monetary authorities reinforced the impression that the G7 meeting will do little aside from calling for stable currency rates.
In particular, U.S. monetary authorities have not shown any signs of changing their stance that a strong dollar is in the best interests of the United States.

Earlier this week, Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin brushed aside U.S. exporters' complaints about the strength of the dollar, saying that the U.S. should not use dollar as an instrument of trade policy.
